page: Amazon Web Services t3.2xlarge is a burstable performance instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon 8259CL cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at 2.5 GHz and includes 35 MB of L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA. It is configured with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or dedicated GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Performance benchmarks reflect its burstable nature and hardware tier. In multi-core stress-ng tests, PassMark CPU evaluations, and Redis SET operations, the instance achieves average performance. However, single-core metrics, including Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core tests, fall into the weak or poor categories. Memory bandwidth read tests and static web serving throughput also register in the bottom 25%, though memory write bandwidth for large blocks maintains average performance.

The t3.2xlarge offers a cost-effective resource density for workloads with variable CPU utilization. Because it uses a burstable CPU allocation model, it is highly efficient for applications that experience periodic spikes but remain idle or low-demand otherwise. The primary tradeoff is the CPU credit system; sustained high-compute workloads will deplete credits, leading to baseline performance throttling unless configured for unlimited credits, which alters the cost profile.

This instance is suited for general-purpose workloads with bursty CPU demands. Appropriate use cases include development and staging environments, code compilation, low-to-medium traffic web serving, and microservices. It is also suitable for small-scale database operations and background task processing that do not require continuous high-throughput CPU or high-speed local storage.
description: Amazon Web Services t3.2xlarge is a burstable x86_64 instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 4 physical Intel Xeon 8259CL cores operating at 2.5 GHz. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory, 35 MB of L3 cache, and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, with no local storage or GPUs. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance utilizes a burstable CPU allocation model. Benchmarks show average multi-core CPU and memory write performance, but weak single-core and memory read speeds. This profile offers a cost-effective option for workloads with variable CPU demands. It is best suited for development environments, code compilation, low-to-medium traffic web servers, and background processing tasks that benefit from burst capacity without requiring sustained, continuous compute power.
